explanations: luna: The verse makes earth a bed and heaven a canopy for people, the same below-and-above arrangement the source draws from earth and sky. | terra: God makes the earth a bed and the sky a building, a habitable above-and-below order close to the section's visible vertical world.
luna: Garden fruit is repeatedly provided in 2:25; that abundant provision clarifies the opposite of the source's food that cannot ease hunger.
terra: Iblis refuses the commanded prostration and وَاسْتَكْبَرَ; unwillingness to lower himself is precisely his culpable self-height.

luna: Here help comes through patience and prayer and is easy only for the خَاشِعِينَ; 2:46 supplies their expectation of meeting and returning to God, linking chosen humility to judgment. | terra: Prayer is called weighty except for الْخَاشِعِينَ, linking willing humility to the endurance that prevents later abasement.
terra: The humble people named in 2:45 are those who expect to meet their Lord and return to Him, linking voluntary humility to the same final return that exposes forced abasement.

luna: After a dispute over food, the people are struck with ذِلَّةٌ and misery; this concretely joins the source's low-food/abasement association while showing refusal of provision ending in humiliation.
terra: The Mount is raised above Israel as they take the covenant, an earlier occurrence of divinely lifted height over accountable people.
terra: The Mount is again raised above Israel when their covenant is taken, repeating the same imposed vertical relation.
luna: Abraham and Ishmael raise the foundations of the House in 2:127; the source's root ر ف ع also names an upward act, here used for a sacred structure.

luna: When told to fear God, the arrogant person is carried by pride into sin and Hell; this ties the source's self-greatening sense of ك ب ر to its great punishment. | terra: When admonished, the wrongdoer is seized by sinful pride; Hell suffices him, a concise nonlexical statement of self-height opening onto punishment.

luna: God raised some messengers over others in degrees; this repeats the source's raised-status root as an act assigned by God. | terra: God favors messengers differently and raises some in degrees, another explicit case of rank being conferred rather than seized.
terra: وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ reserves true exaltedness and immensity for the One whose Throne spans heaven and earth.
terra: The spending parable is جَنَّةٍ بِرَبْوَةٍ, a garden on elevated ground whose doubled yield makes height a received fertility rather than a social claim.

luna: The verse says God gives honor and ذِلَّةٌ to whom He wills; it makes the source's raised status the Lord's gift, not a height a person claims for himself. | terra: تُعِزُّ مَن تَشَاءُ وَتُذِلُّ مَن تَشَاءُ assigns both honor and abasement to God's giving, the governing claim of the section.

luna: God says He will رَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ to Jesus; this is a personal elevation attributed to God rather than self-claim. | terra: God promises Jesus وَرَافِعُكَ إِلَيَّ, using physical elevation as a divine rescue and honor.
terra: The Day when some faces whiten and others blacken restages the section's opposed human countenances, with the darkened group told to taste punishment.
terra: Those whose faces whiten remain in God's mercy, completing 3:106's face contrast with the honored side of the judgment scene.
terra: وَأَنتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ addresses believers after defeat with a conditioned, God-given upper standing rather than worldly boasting.
luna: Some People of the Book are described as خَاشِعِينَ لله while believing revelation; this uses the source's humility root for reverence rather than humiliation.
terra: إِنَّ اللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيًّا كَبِيرًا closes a warning against seeking advantage over another person, placing ultimate height and greatness with God.
terra: Hypocrites occupy الدَّرْكِ الْأَسْفَلِ of the Fire, the spatial opposite of the high garden.
terra: God raises the Mount above them for their covenant, joining physical elevation to commanded submission.
terra: بَل رَّفَعَهُ اللَّهُ إِلَيْهِ makes Jesus's ascent explicitly God's act and therefore an instance of bestowed elevation.
terra: Those who disdain and act arrogantly are promised painful punishment and no protecting ally, directly stating the consequence developed in the section.
terra: Believers are أَذِلَّةٍ toward believers and أَعِزَّةٍ toward rejecters; chosen humility and principled strength replace a single social ladder.

luna: The source's dictionary note for root ض ر ع includes abasement; 6:42 uses يَتَضَرَّعُونَ for people whom hardship might bring to humble supplication. | terra: Hardship is sent لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ, using the food-root's human sense for being brought low enough to implore God.

luna: When punishment arrives, 6:43 asks why they did not يَتَضَرَّعُوا; it turns the source's link between abasement and suffering into a missed chance to humble oneself. | terra: They fail to تَضَرَّعُوا when distress comes because their hearts harden, showing refusal of salutary lowering before punitive lowering.
terra: The messenger is forbidden to drive away the devoted poor whom the surrounding audience devalues; human beings may not be assigned the low place that belongs to service objects.
terra: The privileged ask whether these are the people God favored among them, exposing social rank as a test and divine favor as the real elevation.

luna: The source's dictionary note for root ض ر ع links it to abasement; 6:63 says people call on God تَضَرُّعًا when endangered at sea, a concrete humility under distress. | terra: People invoke God تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً in the darkness of land and sea, using the named food-root's human sense of lowly entreaty.

luna: God says He raises whom He wills in degrees; Abraham's story supplies a human status that comes from God, like the source's gifted height. | terra: نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ makes Abraham's argumentative rank an elevation God grants as He wills.
terra: عَذَابَ الْهُونِ is imposed for false claims about God and arrogance toward His signs, coupling greatness claimed with abasement received.
terra: God says He raised some people above others in degrees as a test, so worldly height is explicitly bestowed and accountable.
terra: أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِّنْهُ gives Iblis's self-ranking logic, which 7:13 answers with descent and inclusion among the abased.
terra: Iblis is told to descend, that arrogance has no place there, and to leave among the abased; self-height becomes imposed lowness.
terra: Those who arrogantly reject God's signs are companions of the Fire, stating the self-height/punishment sequence directly.

luna: The arrogant are barred from the Garden until a camel passes through a needle's eye; the source's pride branch for root ك ب ر thus meets an explicit boundary to its high Garden. | terra: Those who arrogantly reject the signs find heaven's gates closed and the garden impossible to enter, a direct boundary between self-height and the high garden.
terra: The people stationed on the Heights tell recognizable men that their gathering and arrogance did not avail them, exposing claimed rank from an actual high vantage named in 7:46.

luna: The same root ض ر ع appears in the command to call God تَضَرُّعًا and privately; this is chosen humility, set beside the source's imposed abasement. | terra: ادْعُوا رَبَّكُمْ تَضَرُّعًا وَخُفْيَةً commands deliberate humble supplication, the constructive face of becoming low before God.

luna: The same root ض ر ع appears when hardship is sent to a town so its people might يَضَّرَّعُونَ; this repeats abasement as a response to distress. | terra: Prophetic communities are seized by hardship لَعَلَّهُمْ يَضَّرَّعُونَ, another direct use of the named root for human abasement and appeal.

luna: God turns signs away from those who act arrogantly on earth without right; this applies the source's self-exalting sense of ع ل و to a refusal of guidance. | terra: God turns away from His signs those who act arrogantly on earth without right, so self-height itself becomes a cause of lost guidance.
terra: God raises the mountain above the covenant people like a canopy and they think it will fall, making human lowliness visible beneath a divinely lifted height.
terra: God could have raised the man by His signs, but he clung to the earth; bestowed elevation and chosen lowness meet in one sentence.

luna: The source's root ض ر ع also names humility; 7:205 tells the listener to remember and call the Lord تَضَرُّعًا and fearfully, a chosen posture rather than the source's imposed abasement. | terra: God is to be remembered تَضَرُّعًا وَخِيفَةً, making inward abasement a daily practice rather than an imposed final state.
terra: God makes the unbelievers' word السُّفْلَىٰ and His own word الْعُلْيَا, stating the image's vertical reversal as a verdict.
terra: After gardens and fine dwellings are promised, وَرِضْوَانٌ مِّنَ اللَّهِ أَكْبَرُ gives “greater” a positive object beyond even elevated reward.
terra: The people of the garden have faces untouched by darkness or ذِلَّةٌ, the positive boundary opposite the humiliated faces of punishment.
terra: For earners of evil, تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ and darkened faces lead to the Fire, paralleling the section's lowered condemned faces.
terra: No deed escapes God's witnessing and no amount smaller or greater is absent from His record, carrying the named small/great scale into final accountability.

luna: Pharaoh is called لَعَالٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ; the source's dictionary branch for root ع ل و names arrogant domination, and this is its worldly instance. | terra: Pharaoh is described as لَعَالٍ فِي الْأَرْضِ and extravagant, a direct Quranic use of height for tyrannical self-exaltation.
terra: Noah's elite call his followers their lowest people, an arrogant assignment of low human status that the prophetic response refuses.
terra: Noah will not drive believers away because they will meet their Lord, answering the social abasement voiced in 11:27 with their Godward standing.
terra: God makes the overturned city's high part its low part, a literal punitive inversion of عَالِيَهَا and سَافِلَهَا.

luna: In Joseph's story God says نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ; it repeats the source's raising root for rank given by God. | terra: نَرْفَعُ دَرَجَاتٍ مَّن نَّشَاءُ frames Joseph's superior knowledge and plan as bestowed elevation.
terra: Joseph raises his parents onto the throne while they fall in prostration, placing honor and bodily lowering together without confusing either.

luna: God رَفَعَ the heavens without visible pillars in 13:2; this is another direct instance of the source's raising root in the sky. | terra: اللَّهُ الَّذِي رَفَعَ السَّمَاوَاتِ directly attributes the visible height of the heavens to God's raising.
terra: The next verse says He spread the earth and set mountains in it, completing 13:2's raised-sky/extended-earth frame that parallels 88:18–20.
terra: الْكَبِيرُ الْمُتَعَالِ names God as the Great, supremely exalted One, the legitimate union of the two qualities humans counterfeit.
luna: The promised Garden has lasting food and shade in 13:35; this gives the source's high Garden a sustained-provision counterpart.
terra: When all appear before God, the socially weak ask the arrogant whether they can remove any punishment; judgment collapses the hierarchy they maintained.
luna: 15:19 says the earth is spread and plants grow from it; it repeats the source's ground image while connecting the surface to provision.
terra: God removes rancor from the garden's people as they sit like siblings on facing couches, making the seated human position one of conferred reconciliation.
terra: The same destruction turns the city's عَالِيَهَا into سَافِلَهَا, making elevation collapse under judgment.
terra: وَاخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ commands the messenger to lower his wing to believers, a voluntary social lowering opposite pride.
terra: God knows what people conceal and reveal and states that He does not love the arrogant, directly judging the section's self-bestowed height.
terra: The arrogant are told to enter Hell's gates, making the punishment the settled destination of their self-enlargement.
terra: وَلَأَجْرُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ places the greater measure on afterlife reward, the positive counterpart to the section's greatest punishment.

luna: All creatures in the heavens and earth prostrate without arrogance; the source's warning about self-assigned height is bounded by the posture of creation before God. | terra: Everything in the heavens and earth and the angels prostrate to God وَهُمْ لَا يَسْتَكْبِرُونَ; even elevated beings refuse self-height.
terra: The prostrating beings fear their Lord مِن فَوْقِهِمْ and do what they are commanded, completing 16:49's vertical obedience.
luna: The source says the person is seated high while only the cups are placed low; 16:58 shows a daughter's birth treated as disgrace, a human being wrongly pushed into low social standing.

luna: 16:59 makes the social abasement explicit by weighing whether to keep the daughter in humiliation or bury her in dust; it supplies the human-side reversal to the source's placement of objects below honored people.
terra: The highest description belongs to God, marking true elevation as divine while the worst description belongs to those who deny the Hereafter.
terra: عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا combines the section's two secondary roots in Israel's foretold great self-exaltation and corruption.
terra: Worldly ranks are contrasted with the Hereafter, which is أَكْبَرُ دَرَجَاتٍ; its greater degrees clarify the garden's granted elevation.
terra: وَاخْفِضْ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ الذُّلِّ commands a merciful, voluntary lowering before parents, unlike abasement imposed by punishment.

luna: The proud walker cannot split the earth or reach mountains in height; the source's root ع ل و has a self-exalting branch, and this verse sets an explicit limit on it. | terra: The swaggering person on earth is told he can neither split the earth nor reach the mountains in height, so creation itself limits self-importance.
terra: وَتَعَالَىٰ عَمَّا يَقُولُونَ عُلُوًّا كَبِيرًا uses the same “great elevation” language as 17:4 but reserves its true form for God's transcendence.

luna: When revelation is recited, people fall on their chins weeping and their humility increases; this gives the source's root خ ش ع a chosen bodily lowering. | terra: They fall on their chins weeping and revelation increases their خُشُوعًا, giving the root a voluntary bodily descent before God.
luna: The command to magnify God uses the root ك ب ر in reverent glorification; it gives the source's pride branch a clear counterpart in greatness rightly directed to God.
terra: The rewarded believers recline on couches in gardens beneath which rivers flow, another explicit scene of humans honored on garden furnishings.
terra: At judgment the record leaves neither a small nor a great deed uncounted, applying the named small/great opposition to the account behind the greatest punishment.

luna: The verse says Idris was raised to مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا; it combines the source's raising root with a high station given to a person. | terra: وَرَفَعْنَاهُ مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا joins both elevation roots in Idris's God-given high station.
luna: When God's signs are recited, the prophets fall prostrate and weep; this is a chosen low posture, unlike the source's faces lowered by judgment.
terra: Revelation comes from the One who created the earth and the high heavens, stating the section's visible low-and-high cosmic frame in one ayah.
terra: Pharaoh's sorcerers claim success will belong to whoever اسْتَعْلَىٰ, making competitive self-elevation the false premise that 20:68 overturns.
terra: إِنَّكَ أَنتَ الْأَعْلَىٰ gives Moses the upper hand by divine assurance at the moment of fear.
terra: The sorcerers who sought the upper hand in 20:64 are cast down in prostration when truth appears, a bodily reversal that becomes faithful elevation.
terra: Believers who come with righteous deeds receive الدَّرَجَاتُ الْعُلَىٰ, making high ranks a judged reward rather than a self-claim.

luna: On the day people follow the caller, voices are خَشَعَتْ to the Merciful; this carries the source's lowering from faces into the sound of the gathering. | terra: وَخَشَعَتِ الْأَصْوَاتُ lowers all voices before the Merciful in the resurrection gathering, extending bowed faces into bowed sound.
terra: Those who are “with Him” do not act arrogantly toward worship; true nearness and height produce service rather than self-enlargement.
luna: The sky is a protected ceiling in 21:32; this gives the source's raised-heaven image a boundary and sheltering function above the earth.

luna: Zechariah's family hasten to good works, call on God in hope and fear, and are خَاشِعِينَ to Him; this gives the source's lowered-face root a voluntary devotional form. | terra: The prophetic family hastens to good works, calls in hope and fear, and remains humble before God; chosen humility accompanies received divine favor.
terra: Sky, earth, sun, moon, stars, mountains and creatures prostrate, and whoever God humiliates has none to honor him; cosmic lowering and human rank share one divine judgment.
terra: أَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ joins true height and greatness in God, setting the boundary for the section's warning about human self-greatness.
luna: God holds the sky from falling on earth except by His permission; this specifies the boundary between the source's upper sky and lower ground.

luna: The source uses root خ ش ع for faces humbled on judgment day; 23:2 calls believers خَاشِعُونَ in prayer, showing chosen humility before the forced lowering of 88:2. | terra: Successful believers are فِي صَلَاتِهِمْ خَاشِعُونَ, a chosen humility whose outcome contrasts with forced humiliation on the Day.
terra: Pharaoh and his chiefs are قَوْمًا عَالِينَ, using the section's height root for an oppressive people's social self-exaltation.
terra: Mary and Jesus are given refuge on a رَبْوَةٍ with secure rest and flowing water, another beneficent elevated place supplied by God.

luna: Despite punishment, people do not humble themselves to their Lord or تَضَرَّعُوا in 23:76; it repeats the source's root while showing resistance to the abasement meant to turn them back. | terra: Punishment does not make them submit to their Lord and وَمَا يَتَضَرَّعُونَ, so their refusal to lower themselves persists.

luna: The source's root ر ف ع is used for houses God permits to be raised; here elevation marks a consecrated place where His name is remembered. | terra: God permits certain houses أَن تُرْفَعَ and His name to be remembered there, joining elevation with worship rather than status-seeking.
terra: لَقَدِ اسْتَكْبَرُوا فِي أَنفُسِهِمْ وَعَتَوْا عُتُوًّا كَبِيرًا gives self-enlargement and great insolence the section's exact secondary sense.

luna: The servants of the Merciful walk on earth هَوْنًا; this embodied lowliness contrasts with self-given elevation and the humility imposed in the source's judgment scene. | terra: The servants of the Merciful walk gently upon the earth, making lowly bodily comportment the mark of honored servants rather than humiliation.
terra: Noah's opponents object that the lowest people follow him, repeating the social misuse of vertical rank against believers.
terra: Noah refuses to drive the believers away, denying the human ranking asserted in 26:111.
terra: وَاخْفِضْ جَنَاحَكَ similarly directs merciful lowering toward the believers who follow, giving honor through humility.

luna: Pharaoh's people reject signs despite inward certainty, ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا; the source's highness-to-arrogance branch fits this self-raised stance. | terra: Pharaoh's people deny signs ظُلْمًا وَعُلُوًّا despite inward certainty, locating “height” in willful domination.
terra: إِنَّ فِرْعَوْنَ عَلَا فِي الْأَرْضِ immediately unfolds as division and oppression, defining the root's tyrannical secondary face.
terra: Pharaoh orders a baked-brick tower so he might look toward Moses's God, staging arrogant self-raising against the heaven God raised.
terra: Pharaoh and his troops act arrogantly in the earth without right and suppose they will not return, the posture that precedes divine lowering.
terra: God seizes Pharaoh and his troops and casts them into the sea, physically reversing the earthly arrogance named in 28:39.

luna: The Hereafter's home belongs to those who do not desire عُلُوًّا in the land or corruption; this makes the source's Garden elevation a gift for those who refuse self-elevation. | terra: The final home is assigned to those who do not seek عُلُوًّا in the earth, directly opposing self-awarded height to received afterlife height.
terra: Qārūn, Pharaoh and Haman act arrogantly in the earth yet cannot outstrip God, denying their presumed height any escape.
terra: Each arrogant party of 29:39 is then seized for its sin by storm, blast, sinking or drowning, supplying the differentiated lowering.
terra: The highest description in the heavens and earth belongs to God, reserving true height within the whole vertical cosmos for Him.
terra: A hearer turns away arrogantly from God's verses and is promised painful punishment in the same ayah, directly joining self-height to its end.
terra: God creates the heavens without visible pillars and fixes mountains in the earth, another concrete staging of the ordered world above and below.

luna: The verse forbids turning one's cheek away in contempt and walking proudly on earth; it makes bodily haughtiness the chosen inverse of the source's lowered face. | terra: The command forbids turning one's cheek toward people and walking exultantly on earth because God does not love the proud boaster; bodily self-height is checked by the ground beneath it.
terra: Moderating one's walk and lowering one's voice give voluntary daily forms to the descent that punishment otherwise imposes.

luna: The verse calls God الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ, joining the source's named roots ع ل و and ك ب ر as divine attributes rather than human self-elevation. | terra: الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ again belongs to God after false deities are declared false, defining legitimate elevation and greatness.
luna: Those who believe in God's signs fall prostrate and are not arrogant; this links voluntary lowering to the refusal of self-elevation that the source contrasts with the humiliated end.

luna: The verse sets العَذَابَ الأَدْنَىٰ before العَذَابِ الأَكْبَرِ; this directly matches the source's reading of the greater punishment against a lesser, earlier stage. | terra: الْعَذَابِ الْأَدْنَىٰ is set below الْعَذَابِ الْأَكْبَرِ, making the lesser warning and greatest final punishment explicit.

luna: The faithful women and men are among the خَاشِعِينَ; the same root that describes the source's lowered faces can name a chosen quality of worship. | terra: Humble men and women stand among those promised forgiveness and a great reward, linking willing humility to bestowed honor.
terra: Deniers of the Hour are told that nothing smaller or greater than an atom escapes the clear record, joining the small/great scale to resurrection and account.
terra: The heavenly intercession scene ends with وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ, reserving highness and greatness for the One above the fearful servants.
terra: Before their Lord, the weak tell the arrogant that without them they would have believed; the Day exposes the earthly high-and-low hierarchy.
terra: The weak answer the arrogant by naming their schemes, and both conceal regret when punishment and chains appear; manufactured rank ends in shared restraint.

luna: The source's root ر ف ع appears in the good word that ascends and the righteous deed God يَرْفَعُهُ; height here follows worshipful action rather than self-exaltation. | terra: Whoever seeks honor is directed to God: good speech ascends and righteous action raises it, replacing self-exaltation with a Godward ascent.
terra: Arrogance on earth and evil plotting recoil on their own people, making self-elevation carry its own reversal.
terra: The garden's people and their spouses recline in shade on couches, placing human rest and honor at the center of the scene.
terra: They respond to the command of divine unity with arrogance, identifying the stance that leads into the punishment announced nearby.
terra: ذَائِقُو الْعَذَابِ الْأَلِيمِ gives the consequence of the arrogance named in 37:35.

luna: The Garden's people sit facing one another on couches in 37:44; this repeats the source's elevated seat as a setting for companionship. | terra: The sincere servants sit عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ facing one another, and 37:45 then brings a cup around to them.
terra: A cup from a flowing spring is circulated among the people on couches in 37:44, matching the serving-vessel relation.
terra: Those who sought to overcome Abraham are made الْأَسْفَلِينَ, a reversal from intended superiority to lowest position.

luna: Iblis is said to have اِسْتَكْبَرَ; the source's dictionary root ك ب ر includes self-greatening pride, and this refusal turns elevation into rebellion. | terra: All the angels prostrate except Iblis, who acts arrogantly; the verse again stages chosen bodily lowering against self-enlargement.

luna: The question أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعَالِينَ joins pride to being among the high; it directly echoes the source's two branches for ع ل و and ك ب ر. | terra: أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ الْعَالِينَ places arrogant self-enlargement and being among “the high” side by side in God's question to Iblis.
luna: Iblis says he is better because he was made from fire and Adam from clay; this states the self-ranking behind the source's warning about height claimed by a person.
luna: The command فَاخْرُجْ مِنْهَا orders Iblis out after his pride; it makes the fall from self-claimed rank explicit.
terra: After disgrace in the nearer life, وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ makes the greater afterlife punishment the upper term of the same scale.
terra: The condemned self is reminded that God's signs came but it denied them and acted arrogantly, supplying the cause of the blackened proud faces in 39:60.

luna: 39:60 joins darkened faces with the home of the مُتَكَبِّرِينَ; it fuses the source's lowered face and its warning about pride. | terra: The Day shows the faces of those who acted arrogantly blackened and names Hell as their lodging, joining self-height to facial abasement.
terra: The arrogant are ordered through Hell's gates to remain there, repeating the Quran's explicit formula that their self-height ends in the worst lodging.
terra: At judgment the rejecters learn that God's abhorrence when they refused faith was greater than their present self-abhorrence, giving “greater” a punitive scale of reversal.
terra: Judgment belongs to اللَّهِ الْوَاحِدِ الْقَهَّارِ, الْعَلِيِّ الْكَبِيرِ; divine height and greatness stand over those who denied Him alone.

luna: God is رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ and sends warning of the meeting day; this places true height with the Lord who grants it. | terra: رَفِيعُ الدَّرَجَاتِ ذُو الْعَرْشِ locates the possession of high degrees and the Throne in God before the warning of the meeting Day.
terra: Disputing God's signs without authority causes God to seal every arrogant tyrant's heart, a specific inward consequence of self-greatness.
terra: Pharaoh orders Haman to build him a tower, turning his self-elevation into an attempted structure of ascent.
terra: Pharaoh wants the tower's routes to reach the heavens, but the verse calls his scheme ruinous; fabricated ascent cannot reach divine height.
terra: In the Fire, the weak ask the arrogant to relieve a share of punishment; their plea sets up 40:48's admission that all ranks are now together under judgment.
terra: The formerly arrogant tell the formerly weak that all are together in the Fire, where judgment erases their manufactured hierarchy.
terra: The pride in disputants' breasts is مَا هُم بِبَالِغِيهِ, a self-imagined greatness they will never attain.

luna: Those too proud to worship enter Hell دَاخِرِينَ; the source's root ك ب ر self-aggrandizement ends in the humiliation opposed to its raised Garden. | terra: Those too arrogant to worship God will enter Hell دَاخِرِينَ, so their attempted height ends in abased entry.

luna: God makes earth a settled place and heaven a structure; this repeats the source's visible lower-ground/upper-sky relation. | terra: God makes the earth a settled place and the sky a structure, then fashions human forms well; the vertical order is explicitly His provision.
terra: The people in the Fire are told their fate follows wrongful exultation and insolence on earth, immediately explaining the arrogant lodging named in 40:76.
terra: The arrogant are ordered into Hell's gates to abide there, a second exact formulation of self-elevation ending in a debased home.
terra: ʿĀd act arrogantly and ask who is stronger than they, turning self-height into an explicit contest with their Creator.
terra: The humiliating wind-punishment answers ʿĀd's boast in 41:15 and says the afterlife punishment is still more humiliating.

luna: The source's root خ ش ع describes lowered faces; 41:39 calls the earth خَاشِعَةً before rain stirs it and revives it, joining the same root to an earth-to-life reversal. | terra: The earth is seen خَاشِعَةً, then rain makes it stir and swell; a visibly low, still earth rises by God's gift.
terra: He owns what is in heaven and earth and is الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ, grounding the section's vertical world in divine, not human, height.

luna: The wrongdoers stand exposed to the Fire, خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ; this directly joins the source's bowed face to humiliation before punishment. | terra: The wrongdoers are shown before the Fire خَاشِعِينَ مِنَ الذُّلِّ, the same eschatological lowering of persons by humiliation.
terra: The Quran is described as high and wise in the Mother of the Book with God, another elevation granted by divine placement rather than seized.

luna: God apportions livelihoods and يَرْفَعُ بَعْضَهُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ; this gives the source's high place a worldly parallel as an allocated rank. | terra: God says He raised some people above others in degrees so they may employ one another in service, linking given rank with service rather than inherent worth.

luna: The source places أكواب low in a Garden where people sit high; 43:71 has golden dishes and cups circulated among the people, showing vessels as service for their occupants. | terra: Golden dishes and cups are carried around the garden's people, so vessels serve rather than mark a low human rank.
luna: The Garden's people have abundant fruit to eat in 43:73; this adds a specific food-side counterpart to the source's punitive food.
terra: Pharaoh is عَالِيًا among the transgressors, while 44:30 names Israel's rescue from his humiliating punishment.
luna: The tree of زَقُّوم is named as the food of the sinner in 44:43, a direct Hell-food parallel to the source.
luna: 44:44 says this is طَعَامُ الأَثِيمِ, specifying the condemned eater as the source's Hell-food scene does.
luna: The food boils like molten substance in the belly in 44:45, intensifying the bodily suffering attached to the source's thorn food.

luna: The address ذُقْ إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْعَزِيزُ الْكَرِيمُ mocks the condemned person's claimed greatness; the source's dictionary root ك ب ر also carries self-aggrandizement, now answered by punishment.
terra: The person hears God's verses, persists arrogantly as if unheard, and is promised painful punishment in the same ayah.
terra: Rejecters are reminded that the signs were recited but they acted arrogantly and became criminals, immediately before their final exclusion.
terra: وَلَهُ الْكِبْرِيَاءُ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ assigns grandeur throughout the section's high-and-low cosmos to God alone.
terra: Because people acted arrogantly on earth, they receive عَذَابَ الْهُونِ; earthly self-elevation is repaid as humiliating punishment.
terra: وَأَنتُمُ الْأَعْلَوْنَ assures believers of the upper position while God is with them, locating their height in divine accompaniment.

luna: People are made nations to know one another and the most honored before God is the most mindful; this replaces self-awarded rank with a measure from God, like the source's granted Garden elevation.

luna: The built sky is above the people in 50:6; 50:7 completes the view with the spread earth, matching the source's vertical pair. | terra: The audience is told to look at the sky above, how God built and adorned it; 50:7 turns next to the outspread earth.

luna: 50:7 says the earth was spread and set with mountains and growth; 50:6 supplies the sky above it, completing the source's cosmic contrast. | terra: The earth is extended and mountains cast into it beneath the sky of 50:6, paralleling the created sequence in 88:18–20.

luna: The heaven is built with power in 51:47; 51:48 completes the image with the earth spread, recalling the source's raised heaven and lower earth. | terra: The sky is built with power and made vast, while the next verse spreads the earth beneath it.

luna: The earth is spread in 51:48; its paired sky-building in 51:47 supplies the above counterpart to the source's cosmic arrangement. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا completes 51:47's sky with an earth spread like a furnishing below.

luna: The sky is called السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ, a raised roof; this repeats the source's raising image beyond its raised couches. | terra: The oath by السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ presents the heaven as a raised roof, another expression of visible height made by God.

luna: The righteous recline on arranged couches in the Garden, repeating the source's human place of honor above the placed cups. | terra: The God-fearing recline عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ arranged in rows, while 52:23 has them pass a cup among themselves.
luna: The Garden's people are supplied with fruit and meat in 52:22, reinforcing the source's contrast between provision and deprivation.
terra: They pass a cup in the garden without idle or sinful speech, supplying the active service object beside the couches of 52:20.

luna: At resurrection eyes are خُشَّعًا as people leave their graves like scattered locusts; the scene repeats the lowered gaze of 88:2. | terra: خُشَّعًا أَبْصَارُهُمْ shows lowered eyes as people emerge from graves toward the caller on the Day.
luna: After humbled eyes and emergence from graves in 54:7, 54:8 has people hasten toward the caller and call it a difficult day; it completes the source's resurrection posture.
terra: Every small and great matter is inscribed, repeating the size opposition behind “greatest” within a judgment record.

luna: God رَفَعَ the heaven and وَضَعَ the balance; the source names both raising and placing roots for couches and cups, and this verse pairs their opposite actions. | terra: The same verse says God raised the sky and وَوَضَعَ the balance, joining the section's roots for raising and placing in a divinely ordered cosmos.

luna: The earth is وَضَعَهَا for living beings in 55:10; it gives the source's raised sky and low-placed furnishings a grounded counterpart. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ answers the raised sky of 55:7 with an earth laid down for creatures.

luna: Recliners rest on lined couches while the fruit of the two Gardens is near; this develops the source's elevated seating with bounty brought within reach. | terra: The garden's people recline on richly lined furnishings while the fruits of both gardens are near, again lowering provision toward honored occupants.
terra: إِذَا وَقَعَتِ الْوَاقِعَةُ announces the event whose own action is specified as lowering and raising in 56:3.

luna: The source connects a high garden and lowly faces; 56:3 names the Hour as خَافِضَةٌ رَافِعَةٌ, the day that lowers some and raises others. | terra: خَافِضَةٌ رَّافِعَةٌ names the Resurrection itself by the section's two opposed motions: it lowers and raises.

luna: The earlier Garden group reclines on woven سرر; this adds a parallel elevated-seat scene to the source's raised couches. | terra: The foremost are upon woven couches, beginning the same garden arrangement that leads to serving youths and cups in 56:17–18.

luna: The Garden's group sits facing one another on couches in 56:16; this continues the source's raised-seat scene with its social arrangement. | terra: They recline facing one another on the couches of 56:15, defining the human position served in the following verses.
terra: Everlasting youths circulate among the garden's people, establishing the serving relation whose vessels are named in 56:18.

luna: The people of the Garden receive cups, pitchers, and a cup from a flowing spring; it repeats the source's cup imagery as provision. | terra: The circulating youths carry cups, pitchers and a filled cup, directly repeating the garden image of drinking vessels serving honored people.
luna: The Garden group receives chosen fruit in 56:20, the provision-side counterpart to the source's Hell food.
luna: They also receive bird meat as desired in 56:21; this sets satisfying Garden food beside the source's unsatisfying meal.

luna: The source's raised couches use root ر ف ع; 56:34 describes the Garden's beds as مَرْفُوعَةٍ, a close furniture parallel. | terra: وَفُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ repeats the scene of raised furnishings within the garden's reward.
luna: The people of the left are in scorching wind and boiling water; this repeats the source's hot, exposed punishment scene.
luna: 56:43 adds shade of black smoke, extending the environment surrounding the source's Hell food and heat.
luna: That shade is neither cool nor beneficial in 56:44; the verse reinforces the source's absence of relief.
luna: Those punished are told they will eat from the tree of زَقُّوم; this parallels the source's Hell-side thorn food.
luna: The condemned fill their bellies from that tree in 56:53, giving the source's food that cannot relieve hunger a more explicit counterpart.
luna: The meal is followed by الحَمِيم in 56:54, matching the source's hot spring and punitive provision.
luna: They drink like parched camels in 56:55; this makes thirst persist after the source's food fails to relieve hunger.

luna: The verse asks whether believers' hearts should خَشَعَتْ to God's remembrance; the source's humbled face is an imposed end-state, while this is a requested, living response to God. | terra: The faithful are asked whether it is time for their hearts to تَخْشَعَ to God's remembrance, turning lowering inward before it appears on faces.
luna: God says not to grieve over what is missed or exult over what He gives, since He dislikes the boastful; this directly limits the self-awarded elevation warned of in the source.

luna: The source names root ر ف ع for raised couches; in a gathering where people are told to rise, God يَرْفَعِ the believers, making elevation a divine gift. | terra: يَرْفَعِ اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا makes elevation God's response to believers who make room and rise when commanded.
terra: A mountain, the world's conspicuous height, would become خَاشِعًا and split from fear of God if it received the Quran.

luna: The root ك ب ر appears in God's name الْمُتَكَبِّرُ; this locates true greatness with God and bounds the source's warning about people claiming height for themselves. | terra: الْمُتَكَبِّرُ appears as a divine name among God's names, marking the boundary between rightful divine greatness and blameworthy creaturely arrogance.
terra: The hypocrites claim the “mightier” will expel the “lowlier,” but the verse reserves true might for God, His messenger and believers.
terra: وَلَعَذَابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ generalizes the ruined garden owners' worldly punishment into the greater punishment beyond it.
luna: People are called to prostrate but cannot in 68:42; 68:43 names their humbled eyes and disgrace, making refusal the immediate cause of the source-like abasement.

luna: The source's خ ش ع face detail returns with eyes lowered and disgrace; 68:42 supplies the failed call to prostrate, so this verse shows abasement after a rejected summons. | terra: خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ تَرْهَقُهُمْ ذِلَّةٌ exactly binds lowered eyes to the humiliation that overtakes them.
luna: Earth and mountains are lifted and crushed in one blow; this turns the source's ordered high sky and spread earth into a judgment-time upheaval.
luna: The sky splits on that day in 69:16; this reverses the source's raised, stable heaven at the end.

luna: The source identifies root ع ل و in the high garden; 69:22 uses the same phrase, جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ, in a parallel description of the Garden. | terra: فِي جَنَّةٍ عَالِيَةٍ is the exact high-garden scene of 88:10 in another judgment tableau.

luna: After its high Garden, 69:23 says its fruit is دَانِيَةٌ, near at hand; height and accessible low-hanging provision coexist in one scene. | terra: The fruit clusters hang دَانِيَةٌ inside the high garden of 69:22, so what serves its honored people is brought low and near.
luna: The blessed are told to eat and drink in enjoyment for what they sent ahead; this ties Garden provision to deeds, against the source's punitive food.
luna: For the condemned there is no food except غِسْلِين in 69:36; this repeats the source's deprivation through a different Hell food.
luna: 69:37 restricts that food to sinners, completing the source's distinction between punitive and Garden provision.
luna: 70:43 shows people emerging rapidly from graves toward the caller; 70:44 supplies the humbled eyes, so this verse adds the movement into the source's judgment scene.

luna: The source section names root خ ش ع for lowered faces; 70:44 again gives humbled eyes and surrounding humiliation on that day, matching 88:2. | terra: The promised Day is again marked by خَاشِعَةً أَبْصَارُهُمْ and enveloping humiliation, directly echoing the section's bowed faces.
terra: Noah's people persist and act arrogantly with emphatic arrogance, a concentrated statement of the self-height that resists saving remembrance.
luna: Seven heavens are created in layers in 71:15; this gives the source's raised sky a visible vertical structure.
luna: God makes the earth بُسَاطًا for people in 71:19; this supplies the lower, traversable counterpart to the source's layered heavens.

luna: The person who turns away and اِسْتَكْبَرَ displays the source's secondary ك ب ر sense; 74:26 supplies the threat of Saqar, while this verse contributes the arrogant response. | terra: ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ وَاسْتَكْبَرَ marks the self-enlarging turn that precedes the threat of Saqar.

luna: Saqar is the punishment announced after the arrogant rejection in 74:23; this verse supplies the fire-side consequence to the source's great-punishment link. | terra: سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ supplies the fiery end of the arrogance in 74:23.

luna: 75:22 gives radiant faces on that day, a positive counterpart to 88:2's humbled faces. | terra: Some faces on that Day are radiant, supplying the elevated side of the face-pair opposite humbled, darkened faces.

luna: The radiant faces in 75:22 look toward their Lord in 75:23; this adds their stance to the source's contrast between abasement and Garden honor. | terra: The radiant faces of 75:22 look toward their Lord, giving that honored face-state its own Godward orientation.

luna: 75:24 turns to other faces, بَاسِرَةٌ, on that same day; the passage again divides faces into opposite outcomes. | terra: Other faces on that Day are grim, the corresponding condemned side of the eschatological face-pair.

luna: Those faces expect a back-breaking disaster in 75:25, clarifying why the source's lowered face belongs to a punitive scene. | terra: The grim faces of 75:24 expect a crushing calamity, supplying their own awareness of the punitive side of the face contrast.
luna: God shields people from that day's evil and gives them نَضْرَةً وَسُرُورًا; this contrasts the source's humbled faces with the Garden's radiant, joyful outcome.

luna: The Garden's people recline on couches, protected from sun and cold; this expands the source's raised resting place into an environment of ease. | terra: The garden's people recline on couches while the following verses lower shade and fruit and bring vessels to them, establishing the honored human position.

luna: The Garden's shade covers its people and its fruit is made readily accessible; the low reach of the fruit complements the source's high Garden and raised seating. | terra: Garden shade is brought near and its fruit is made submissively low, matching the section's low service objects beneath honored occupants.

luna: Here silver vessels and أكواب are carried around the Garden's people; the source's set cups and raised couches become a fuller serving scene. | terra: Silver vessels and cups are circulated among the reclining people, directly enacting the section's service-cup detail.
luna: The Garden's drink is mixed with ginger in 76:17; this develops the cup service parallel to the source's placed vessels.
luna: The drink comes from a spring called Salsabil in 76:18; this adds a Garden spring to the source's cups and high seating.
luna: Young attendants circulate among the Garden's people in 76:19; this makes explicit the service relation implicit in the source's low-placed cups and honored occupants.
luna: God makes earth مِهَادًا in 78:6; the later heavens above in 78:12 complete a lower-ground/upper-sky arrangement like the source's.
luna: 78:12 describes seven strong heavens above people; 78:6 supplies the earth made a resting place, completing the source's vertical pair.
luna: The Hell-dwellers taste neither coolness nor drink in 78:24; this clarifies the deprivation behind the source's food that cannot satisfy hunger.
luna: Their only drink is حَمِيم and غَسَّاق in 78:25, a close counterpart to the source's boiling spring.
luna: Hearts tremble in 79:8, and 79:9 supplies the humbled eyes; this verse identifies the inner fear behind the source's lowered face.

luna: The day of trembling hearts has eyes خَاشِعَةٌ; the source's lowered-face root thus appears again in the bodily fear of judgment. | terra: أَبْصَارُهَا خَاشِعَةٌ gives the terrified resurrection scene the same downcast gaze.

luna: The source's dictionary root ع ل و includes arrogant self-exaltation; Pharaoh's claim أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَىٰ is its sharpest self-awarded height. | terra: Pharaoh's أَنَا رَبُّكُمُ الْأَعْلَىٰ is the extreme form of a human giving himself the height that belongs to God.

luna: The next verse says God seized Pharaoh as a warning for this life and the next; it completes the source's movement from claimed height to punishment. | terra: God's seizure of Pharaoh in punishment for the last and first offense supplies the immediate answer to his claim of being “highest” in 79:24.

luna: The source names root ر ف ع and the sky's height; 79:28 says God raised its ceiling and proportioned it, a direct cosmic raising. | terra: رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا describes God raising the sky's structure, a direct counterpart to 88:18.

luna: After describing the raised heaven, 79:30 says the earth was spread; this gives the source's high sky and low earth their paired scene. | terra: وَالْأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ دَحَاهَا completes the raised sky of 79:28 with the earth extended below.
luna: The one who transgresses and آثَرَ الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا is the source of the low-life choice set against the raised Garden.
luna: For that transgressor, Hell is the refuge in 79:39; it gives the source's self-elevating turn its punitive destination.
luna: The one who fears standing before the Lord and restrains the soul from desire is the contrasting figure to the source's self-aggrandizing person.
luna: For the restrained soul, the Garden is the refuge; this makes the source's high Garden a granted outcome of fear and restraint.
terra: The purified scripture leaves are مَرْفُوعَةٍ, a non-spatial sacred elevation conferred on the reminder.
luna: The command to let man look at his food opens a provision scene; it sets the source's Hell food against food's ordinary dependence on what God brings forth.
luna: Water is poured out in 80:25; it adds the needed source of nourishment beside the source's boiling spring.
luna: The earth is split open in 80:26 so food can grow; this connects the source's spread-earth scene to sustenance rather than the Hell-side barrenness.
luna: Grain is made to grow in 80:27; this contrasts ordinary nourishment with the source's thorn food.
luna: Grapes and fodder follow in 80:28; the sequence shows food and pasture as provision unlike the source's non-nourishing meal.
luna: Olives and palms in 80:29 extend the cultivated food provision that contrasts with the source's deprivation.
luna: Gardens are densely grown in 80:30; the verse adds the fruitful landscape absent from the source's Hell scene.
luna: Greenery and pasture in 80:31 continue the provision list, contrasting with the source's non-nourishing food.
luna: The growth is a provision for people and livestock in 80:32; this states explicitly what the source's Hell food fails to provide.

luna: 80:38 begins the other face-scene with radiant faces on that day, setting the Garden's ease beside the source's lowered faces. | terra: Faces on that Day are bright, beginning another Quranic contrast between honored and abased human countenances.

luna: Those radiant faces laugh and rejoice in 80:39; it fills out the opposite outcome to the source's abasement. | terra: The bright faces of 80:38 laugh and rejoice, completing the honored countenance before the passage turns to abased faces.

luna: 80:40 turns to other faces on that day, now covered with غَبَرَةٌ; the paired faces echo the two outcomes surrounding 88:2. | terra: Other faces on that Day bear dust, a visible lowering that 80:41 completes with darkness.

luna: Those faces are covered by قَتَرَةٌ in 80:41, completing the dark, constricted counterpart to the source's raised Garden scene. | terra: Darkness covers the dust-marked faces of 80:40, completing their visible abasement on the Day.
luna: 80:42 identifies these grim-faced people as the disbelieving sinners; it makes the face-contrast a judgment of response, not just appearance.

luna: The righteous look out from الأرائك in 83:23; this repeats the source's elevated resting place in a Garden. | terra: The righteous sit on couches looking out, combining the garden's honored human position with an elevated viewing stance.

luna: Their faces show نَضْرَةَ النَّعِيمِ in 83:24, a bright-faced contrast to the source's humbled faces. | terra: The radiance of bliss is recognizable in the faces of those on couches in 83:23, joining the section's pleasant faces to its furnishings.
terra: The believers again look out from couches, repeating the garden scene after earthly social roles have been reversed.
luna: At the end, the earth is extended in 84:3; this reverses the source's stable spread-earth scene into the day of judgment.
luna: 84:4 says the earth casts out what is within and becomes empty; it explains the judgment-time extension in 84:3 and turns the source's ground into a scene of disclosure.
luna: The earth listens to and obeys its Lord in 84:5; this completes the extended-earth sequence with submission to the Lord who orders the source's high and low.
terra: The command to glorify رَبِّكَ الْأَعْلَىٰ reserves true highestness for the Lord; 87:12 later answers refusal with the greatest fire.

luna: The condemned enter النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ; the source itself cites this earlier surah's phrase as another use of the root ك ب ر for the greatest punishment. | terra: النَّارَ الْكُبْرَىٰ is the other Quranic “greatest fire,” and its surah has already named God as the Most High in 87:1.
luna: 87:16 says people prefer الْحَيَاةَ الدُّنْيَا; this supplies the low, nearer-life choice behind the source's contrast between granted Garden height and punishment.
luna: The next verse says the Hereafter is خير وأبقى; it completes the boundary between preferred near life and the lasting outcome tied to the source's high Garden and great punishment.
luna: When provision is widened, the person says رَبِّي أَكْرَمَنِ; the verse exposes the self-ranking by material plenty that the source warns against in its height-and-pride turn.
luna: When provision is restricted, the person says رَبِّي أَهَانَنِ; this directly joins food provision to claimed abasement, then the following verses correct that inference.

luna: The oath names the sky and its builder; 91:6 completes it with the spread earth, closely pairing the two elements that the source sets high and low. | terra: The oath by the sky and the One who built it begins another paired view of the visible vertical world.

luna: The earth is spread in 91:6; 91:5 supplies the sky and its builder, completing the source's sky-earth pairing. | terra: The oath by the earth and the One who spread it completes the built-sky/extended-earth pair of 91:5.
terra: ابتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ الْأَعْلَىٰ makes the Most High Lord, not social height, the giver's sole object.
terra: وَرَفَعْنَا لَكَ ذِكْرَكَ presents raised renown as God's gift, another non-spatial form of the section's bestowed height.
terra: Humanity is returned أَسْفَلَ سَافِلِينَ after the finest formation in 95:4, a sharp descent from granted stature.
luna: The earth is shaken violently when the Hour arrives; this makes the source's spread ground undergo an explicit eschatological reversal.
luna: The earth casts out its burdens in 99:2; the next verse has humanity ask what is happening, so this adds the ground's testimony to the source's judgment scene.
